# IAM findings accepted on the RENDERED PLAN scan (deploy-infra.yml), by check ID AND
# resource. Anything not listed here fails the job when GATE_CHECKOV_PLAN=block.
#
# THE LIST IS EMPTY, and that is the current state rather than a placeholder. It held two
# findings on `module.base.aws_iam_role_policy.github_actions_deploy` — CKV_AWS_290 and
# CKV_AWS_355 — until SPEC-202 retired CloudFront and the deploy role's `cloudfront:*`
# statement came off with it. Both were that statement alone, measured against the pinned
# checkov's own scanner rather than argued: with it gone the policy reports zero of either.
#
# The header this replaces named `cognito-idp:CreateUserPool`, `logs:DescribeLogGroups` and
# the Lake Formation account-level actions as co-causes. They are not, and the distinction
# matters for the next grant: those actions ARE unscopable, but cloudsplaining — which both
# checks wrap — does not count an action it already classifies as taking no resource type,
# so an unscopable action alone raises nothing. What raises these two is an action that COULD
# have been scoped and was not. CKV_AWS_355 counts every such action ("restrictable", in its
# own words) — a read or a tagging call fires it exactly as a write does — and CKV_AWS_290
# counts the write subset of the same list. `cognito-identity:CreateIdentityPool` went with
# the Identity Pool in the same spec.
#
# So an empty list means every IAM finding on the plan now fails the job, and the mechanism
# stays because the next grant that needs it will need it in the same shape: accepted by
# check ID AND RESOURCE, never by check ID alone, so the same rule firing on any other policy
# still fails. The USER-FACING ISOLATION policies (`portal-role-permissions` and the
# per-plane control-plane execution roles) have zero `Resource: "*"` and must stay that way.
# That claim is narrowed deliberately: it does not cover every role in the account. The SPA's
# ECS task-execution role holds `ecr:GetAuthorizationToken` on `"*"`, which is unscopable (the
# action takes no resource type at all) and reaches no user data. Its scoped siblings — the
# three pull actions and the two log actions — name the repository and the log group.
#
# A line here that no longer matches a finding is a HARD ERROR — it either describes something
# already fixed, or points at a resource that has been renamed, in which case it is accepting
# nothing while reading as an acceptance. Delete or correct the line. That is what emptied
# this file: the grant went, the acceptances stopped matching, and the gate said so.
#
# This blocks PRs only. The `plan` job runs on pull_request; `apply` runs on push/dispatch and
# does not depend on it, so nothing here can redden a production deploy.
#
# ONE PIECE OF FRICTION WORTH EXPECTING. Adding a wildcard statement to
# `github_actions_deploy` — the recurring case CLAUDE.md's "Infra rule" mandates for any spec
# provisioning new infra — fires CKV_AWS_355 for any scopable action in it, CKV_AWS_290 if
# that action is also a write, and CKV_AWS_63 for `Action: "*"`. Those three are the ones that
# reach this resource. CKV_AWS_356 / CKV_AWS_111 / CKV_AWS_49 are their `aws_iam_policy_document`
# DATA-SOURCE twins and cannot fire on an `aws_iam_role_policy` — measured against the pinned
# checkov, after this file spent a release naming them. So such a change is a two-step edit:
# the grant, and the acceptance for it. Deliberate.
